newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed at close, tracking natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed at close, tracking natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed at the close, with natural gas prices still cited as the main driver behind the market, trade sources said Thursday.
"It's followed natgas up down and all around," said one trader.
But he noted comparatively warmer temperatures and continued abundance of hydroelectric power in the Pacific Northwest may exert some downward pressure on futures prices by early next week.
"Temperatures will even be above normal in some areas by then," agreed another market source.
But he noted as long as natural gas prices hold firm, power prices will not come down.

January 1997 California-Oregon border (COB) futures ended down 14 cents at $26.86 per megawatt hour, while the February contract was up 8 cents at $20.39. Other active COB contracts closed 10 to 60 cents lower.
January Palo Verde was up 15 cents at $27.90, while February lost 5 cents to close at $21.95. Other PV contracts closed between 15 cents higher and 25 cents lower.
